name: Neil Robertson
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2006 Grand Prix at age 24, becoming the first Australian to win a snooker ranking event.
early_history_summary: Robertson first played snooker at age 11 at his family's pool club in Melbourne. He won the Australian under-18 championship at 14, turned professional at 16, and after dropping off the tour and working in a pub, won the World Under-21 Championship in 2003 to regain his tour place. His first ranking title came at the 2006 Grand Prix at age 24.
family_context_summary: Robertson grew up in Melbourne in a family that owned a pool club where he first played snooker at age 11. His father studied the game extensively and helped develop his technique, while his mother made significant sacrifices to support his career relocation to the UK.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father was deeply knowledgeable about snooker technique, studying players like Hendry and Davis, and contributed ideas to Robertson's game throughout his junior career.
primary_early_advantage_tags: family pool club, early specialization, father coaching, left school at 15
evidence_summary: Robertson grew up around his family's pool club in Melbourne, starting snooker at 11 and winning the Australian U-18 title at 14. His father studied the game deeply and contributed to his technique. He left school at 15 to pursue snooker full-time, turned professional at 16, and after setbacks including homesickness and dropping off the tour, won the World U-21 Championship at 21 and his first ranking title at 24. His family made significant sacrifices to support his relocation to the UK.
starting_point: Born in Melbourne, Australia to a family that owned a pool club; father was knowledgeable about snooker and mother worked hard to support the family.
current_position: Active professional snooker player ranked #2 in the world as of 2025; former world champion and Triple Crown winner with 26 ranking titles.

trajectory.event: Won the Australian Under-18 snooker championship and became the youngest player to make a century break in an Australian ranking event.

name: Park Ji-sung
milestone_by_age_26: Signed for Manchester United in July 2005 at age 24, after winning two Eredivisie titles with PSV Eindhoven and reaching the UEFA Champions League semifinals.
early_history_summary: Park began playing football in elementary school in Suwon, South Korea, and progressed through Suwon Technical High School and Myongji University. He debuted for the South Korean national team in 2000 at age 19 and joined Kyoto Purple Sanga in Japan's J-League. He followed national team manager Guus Hiddink to PSV Eindhoven in December 2002, where he won two Eredivisie titles and reached the Champions League semifinals before signing for Manchester United at age 24.
family_context_summary: Park grew up in a working-class family in Suwon, South Korea. His father ran a butcher shop and side dish store, and his parents were not highly educated or wealthy. They initially opposed his football career due to his small stature but eventually supported him.
parent_family_domain_summary: Park's father was athletic and outgoing but had no professional football background. His parents emphasized discipline and self-management, requiring him to be home by 9pm throughout his youth career.
primary_early_advantage_tags: national team pipeline, Hiddink connection, J-League to PSV path, exceptional fitness
evidence_summary: Park grew up in a working-class family in Suwon with no football connections; his father ran a butcher shop. Despite being small and flat-footed, Park progressed through school and university football, debuting for South Korea at 19. The 2002 World Cup and his connection to manager Guus Hiddink catalyzed his move to PSV Eindhoven, where he won two league titles and reached the Champions League semifinals, leading to a Manchester United transfer at 24.
starting_point: Born in Seoul, South Korea to a working-class family in Suwon; father ran a butcher shop and mother was a homemaker; parents were not wealthy or highly educated.
current_position: Retired from professional football in 2014; currently serves as an advisor at Jeonbuk Hyundai Motors; won 19 trophies including 4 Premier League titles and the UEFA Champions League with Manchester United.

name: Jos Verstappen
milestone_by_age_26: Made Formula One debut in 1994 at age 22, scoring two podium finishes (Hungary and Belgium) in his rookie season alongside Michael Schumacher at Benetton.
early_history_summary: Verstappen began karting at age 8 in Dutch Limburg, winning national and European karting titles. He transitioned to car racing in 1992, winning the Formula Opel Lotus Benelux championship, then the German Formula 3 championship in 1993. He was signed as Benetton's test driver for 1994 and was promoted to a race seat when JJ Lehto was injured, making his F1 debut at the Brazilian Grand Prix at age 22.
family_context_summary: Verstappen grew up in Dutch Limburg. He discovered karting at age 8 when he and his father heard engines after leaving church. Family background details are limited in reviewed sources.

He transitioned to car racing in 1992, winning championships in Formula Opel Lotus and German Formula 3 in consecutive years. Manager Huub Rothengatter secured sponsorship from Philips and Marlboro, and Verstappen's F1 test times impressed multiple teams, leading to a Benetton seat in 1994 where he scored two podiums as a 22-year-old rookie.

name: Martin Sheen
milestone_by_age_26: Received a Tony Award nomination for Best Featured Actor in a Play for his Broadway performance in 'The Subject Was Roses' in 1964 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Sheen was drawn to acting as a youth in Dayton, Ohio, despite his father's disapproval. He deliberately failed the entrance exam for the University of Dayton and borrowed money from a Catholic priest to move to New York City in his early twenties. He joined the Living Theatre and had a key featured role in 'The Connection' in 1961 at age 21, leading to his Broadway breakthrough in 'The Subject Was Roses' in 1964.
family_context_summary: Sheen was born Ramón Antonio Gerard Estevez in Dayton, Ohio, to an Irish immigrant mother and a Spanish-born factory worker father. The family was working-class, and his father disapproved of his acting ambitions.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. His father was a factory worker and machinery inspector with no connection to the entertainment industry.

evidence_summary: Sheen grew up in a working-class immigrant family in Dayton, Ohio, with a Spanish-born factory worker father and Irish immigrant mother. Despite his father's opposition, he borrowed money from a Catholic priest to move to New York City and joined the avant-garde Living Theatre. His talent was recognized quickly, leading to a key role in 'The Connection' at 21 and a Tony-nominated Broadway performance in 'The Subject Was Roses' at 24. His working-class background and father's disapproval created urgency rather than support.
starting_point: Born in Dayton, Ohio to a Spanish-born factory worker father and Irish immigrant mother; working-class family with no entertainment connections.
current_position: Still active as an actor at age 85; best known for Apocalypse Now (1979) and The West Wing (1999-2006); has appeared in over 65 feature films.

name: Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo
milestone_by_age_26: Released Daft Punk's debut album 'Homework' in 1997 at age 23, which became a critically acclaimed and commercially successful landmark of the French house movement.
early_history_summary: Homem-Christo met Thomas Bangalter at the Lycée Carnot in Paris in 1987. They formed the indie rock trio Darlin' in 1992 with Laurent Brancowitz, releasing a single on Duophonic Records. After a negative review called their music 'a daft punky thrash,' they formed Daft Punk in 1993, released their first single on Soma Quality Recordings in 1994, and broke through with 'Da Funk' in 1995 and the 'Homework' album in 1997.
family_context_summary: Born in Neuilly-sur-Seine, an affluent suburb of Paris. His parents owned and ran an advertising company together in Paris. He is of Portuguese descent, the great-grandson of Portuguese poet Homem Cristo Filho.
parent_family_domain_summary: His parents ran an advertising company in Paris, providing a comfortable upper-middle-class background. No direct music industry connection is documented, though the advertising and business environment may have provided cultural fluency.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Bangalter partnership, Paris French house scene, Lycée Carnot meeting, affluent background, electronic music wave
evidence_summary: Homem-Christo grew up in affluent Neuilly-sur-Seine with parents who owned an advertising company. He met Thomas Bangalter at Lycée Carnot in Paris in 1987, forming a creative partnership that would define their careers. They experimented with indie rock as Darlin' in 1992, then pivoted to electronic music after attending a rave at EuroDisney in 1993. Their complementary partnership, combined with the Paris French house scene and the 1990s EDM wave, led to the release of 'Homework' in 1997 at age 23, a landmark debut album.
starting_point: Born in Neuilly-sur-Seine, an affluent Paris suburb; parents owned and ran an advertising company; of Portuguese descent, great-grandson of a poet.
current_position: Daft Punk officially split in 2021; Homem-Christo has been producing through his label Crydamoure and collaborating on select projects.

name: Claude Criquielion
milestone_by_age_26: In his neo-professional year of 1979 at age 22, Criquielion achieved a top-10 finish in the Tour de France and won the Setmana Catalana and Escalada a Montjuïc, marking him as one of cycling's rising stars.
early_history_summary: Criquielion grew up on a farm in Lessines, Belgium. His father, a cycling enthusiast, bought him a mini racing bike at age 12 and encouraged him to switch from running to cycling. He won 37 races as a junior and 27 as an amateur, won a stage of the Tour de l'Avenir in 1977 at age 20, and nearly won the 1978 amateur world road race championships before turning professional with KAS in 1979.
